title: RcppOptimLib — Implementation Plan
text: Flat header layout. OptimLib’s headers use include paths relative library root ("misc/optim_structs.hpp", "BaseMatrixOps/include/BaseMatrixOps.hpp"), sit directly inst/include/ — subdirectory. LinkingTo puts exactly one directory (<pkg>/include) compiler search path, layout works client packages without patching every include library. inst/include/RcppOptimLib.h single entry point. defines OPTIM_USE_RCPP_ARMADILLO (OptimLib includes <RcppArmadillo.h> — without flag, RcppArmadillo’s system Armadillo’s configurations mix fail link) OPTIM_DONT_USE_OPENMP, includes optim.hpp. defines live header rather src/Makevars, client packages inherit automatically. OpenMP default. OptimLib auto-enables OpenMP whenever _OPENMP defined, parallel metaheuristics (DE, PSO) evaluate objective worker threads. R’s C API single-threaded, R-function callback objective OpenMP crash session. client package uses pure C++ objectives may opt back defining RCPPOPTIMLIB_ALLOW_OPENMP including RcppOptimLib.h adding $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS) Makevars. Patches vendored code: Index-vector typedefs (marked [RcppOptimLib patch] misc/optim_options.hpp): ColVecUInt_t/RowVecUInt_t changed arma::Col<unsigned long long> arma::Col<arma::uword>. LP64 Linux arma::uword unsigned long, distinct type unsigned long long, Armadillo ≥ 12 index-vector overloads (X.rows(uvec), X(uvec)) reject upstream type. Worth offering upstream PR. Console output: std::cout/std::cerr/printf replaced mechanically (sed) Rcpp::Rcout/Rcpp::Rcerr/Rprintf across headers — CRAN forbids compiled code writing stdout/stderr, R CMD check flags symbols even print paths disabled runtime. Also pruned: BaseMatrixOps/.git, .github/ tests/ (hidden-file NOTE GNU-Makefile WARNING check). unconstrained/lbfgs.hpp: x advanced x_p first line search, first -loop curvature pair used s spanning two steps one-step y; L-BFGS stalled 2 iterations Rosenbrock. first-step grad_err also used initial gradient instead grad_p. unconstrained/pso_dv.hpp: stagnation-reset Hadamard product mixed column vector (rand_vec) row vector (P_max - P_min); Armadillo throws runtime. constrained/sumt.hpp: penalty gradient c * colSums(J) instead c * t(J) %*% g, inconsistent penalized objective; BFGS stalled penalty grew (x + y <= 2 test stopped 1.00046 instead 1). Known upstream behaviours patched, handled R side: de_prmm halves population three times (hard-coded) indexes unsigned arithmetic, n_pop %/% 8 <= n_pop_best reads bounds — optimlib() validates . check_freq = Inf, de reports success n_gen generations de_prmm/pso/pso_dv report failure — documented ?optimlib. de_prmm ignores n_gen (budget comes max_fn_eval pmax) — documented ?optimlib_control. broyden_df without Jacobian can diverge NaN poor starts (e.g. (1, 0.5) x^2 + y^2 = 4, x = y); treated algorithmic, bug — documented ?optimlib_root. Licensing. package GPL (>= 3) (Apache-2.0 compatible GPL-3 GPL-2); bundled OptimLib BaseMatrixOps headers Apache-2.0, Copyright Keith O’Hara, listed Authors@R aut, cph. See inst/COPYRIGHTS, inst/include/optimlib-LICENSE inst/include/optimlib-NOTICE.txt.

what: Phase 2 — a real R-level interface (done on dev-0.0.2)
title: RcppOptimLib — Implementation Plan
text: Implemented R/optimlib.R, R/control.R, R/wrappers.R src/interface.cpp. validation, defaults finite differences R side; C++ entry points (.optimlib_min, .optimlib_sumt, .optimlib_root, unexported) assume complete, validated control list. optimlib(par, fn, gr = NULL, ..., method, lower, upper, hess,     control) ten unconstrained methods: bfgs, lbfgs, cg, gd, newton, nm, de, de_prmm, pso, pso_dv. Box bounds every method except newton (upstream support); par must strictly inside bounds (OptimLib transforms ) optimlib_sumt() (inequality constraints constr(x) <= 0) optimlib_root() (broyden, broyden_df, optional Jacobian) optimlib_control() maps onto optim::algo_settings_t: general tolerances plus one named list per algorithm mirroring OptimLib’s *_settings_t structs; unknown names invalid values errors. cg$method / gd$method accept names ("hz", "adam") upstream integer codes. exposed: omp_n_threads (OpenMP ), NM custom initial simplex, DE/PSO population-matrix return Missing derivatives: central finite differences computed R (gradient; Hessian symmetrized Jacobian gradient; constraint Jacobian SUMT), OptimLib’s numerical helpers RNG: control$seed NULL, stochastic methods draw seed R’s RNG (sample.int), set.seed() gives reproducible results; deterministic methods touch .Random.seed R errors callbacks: Rcpp::Function evaluates unwind protection, R error becomes C++ exception unwinds OptimLib’s frames (hold RAII objects catch blocks) Rcpp export wrapper. Tested (stop("boom"), including first evaluation) Callbacks receive plain numeric vector (0.0.1 passed n x 1 matrix — noted NEWS behaviour change); return lengths dimensions checked C++ informative errors Return classed object (optimlib_result) print() method — currently plain list: par, value, success, iterations, error, method (fn_values instead value root finding)

title: Introduction to RcppOptimLib
text: optimlib() minimizes plain R function OptimLib algorithm, interface modelled optim(). BFGS Rosenbrock function, analytic gradient: Choose algorithm method. Gradient-based methods fall back finite differences gr omitted; Nelder–Mead, differential evolution particle swarm need gradient : Bounds given lower upper. population methods use R’s random number generator seed, set.seed() makes reproducible: control takes general settings (iter_max, tolerances, print_level) per-algorithm lists lbfgs = list(par_M = 20) gd = list(method = "adam"); see ?optimlib_control. Nonlinear inequality constraints g(x) <= 0 handled optimlib_sumt(), systems equations optimlib_root(): Every objective evaluation crosses R/C++ boundary, performance-critical work write objective C++ ().
code: rosenbrock    <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 rosenbrock_gr <- function(x) c(-400 * x[1] * (x[2] - x[1]^2) - 2 * (1 - x[1]),                                 200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)) optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gr) #> $par #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $value #> [1] 2.233623e-18 #>  #> $success #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 31 #>  #> $error #> [1] 4.734761e-09 #>  #> $method #> [1] "bfgs" sapply(c("lbfgs", "cg", "nm"), function(m) {   optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, method = m)$par }) #>      lbfgs cg nm #> [1,]     1  1  1 #> [2,]     1  1  1 set.seed(3016) optimlib(c(2, 2), rosenbrock, method = "de", lower = -5, upper = 5,          control = list(de = list(n_gen = 300)))$par #> [1] 1 1 optimlib_sumt(c(0, 0), function(x) sum((x - 2)^2),               constr = function(x) sum(x^2) - 1)$par #> [1] 0.7071068 0.7071068 optimlib_root(c(1.2, 1.3), function(x) c(sum(x^2) - 4, x[1] - x[2]))$par #> [1] 1.414214 1.414214

code: // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppOptimLib, RcppArmadillo)]] #include <RcppOptimLib.h>  double sphere_fn(const arma::vec& x, arma::vec* grad_out, void*) {     if (grad_out) *grad_out = 2.0 * x;     return arma::dot(x, x); }  // [[Rcpp::export]] Rcpp::List minimize_sphere(arma::vec x0) {     optim::algo_settings_t settings;     bool ok = optim::bfgs(x0, sphere_fn, nullptr, settings);     return Rcpp::List::create(         Rcpp::Named("par") = Rcpp::NumericVector(x0.begin(), x0.end()),         Rcpp::Named("value") = settings.opt_fn_value,         Rcpp::Named("success") = ok); } optim_ackley_de(c(2, -2), seed = 42L) #> $par #> [1]  0.000000e+00 -2.775558e-16 #>  #> $value #> [1] 4.440892e-16 #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 1001 #>  #> $success #> [1] TRUE

title: An Interface to the C++ Numerical Optimization Library OptimLib
text: R interface OptimLib, Keith O’Hara’s header-C++ library numerical optimization methods nonlinear functions — BFGS, L-BFGS, conjugate gradient, gradient descent, Newton, Nelder–Mead, differential evolution, particle swarm, constrained optimization (SUMT) root finding — built Armadillo linear algebra library. OptimLib headers (header-mode) shipped inst/include/, R packages can use adding DESCRIPTION linking BLAS/LAPACK src/Makevars (required Windows): standalone C++ file: R, every algorithm available plain R functions optim()-like interface: See ?optimlib_control convergence algorithm-specific settings. See IMPLEMENTATION.md design decisions development roadmap.
code: LinkingTo: RcppOptimLib, Rcpp, RcppArmadillo PKG_LIBS = $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS) // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppOptimLib, RcppArmadillo)]] #include <RcppOptimLib.h>  double sphere_fn(const arma::vec& x, arma::vec* grad_out, void*) {     if (grad_out) *grad_out = 2.0 * x;     return arma::dot(x, x); }  // [[Rcpp::export]] arma::vec minimize_sphere(arma::vec x0) {     optim::bfgs(x0, sphere_fn, nullptr);     return x0; } rosenbrock    <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 rosenbrock_gr <- function(x) c(-400 * x[1] * (x[2] - x[1]^2) - 2 * (1 - x[1]),                                 200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2))  optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gr)                  # BFGS optimlib(c(-1.2, 1), rosenbrock, method = "lbfgs",               # numeric gradient          control = list(lbfgs = list(par_M = 5))) optimlib(c(0.5, 0.5), rosenbrock, method = "nm",                 # box constraints          lower = 0, upper = 0.8)  set.seed(1)                                                       # global search optimlib(c(2, 2), rosenbrock, method = "pso", lower = -5, upper = 5)  optimlib_sumt(c(0, 0), function(x) sum((x - 2)^2),                # x1 + x2 <= 2               constr = function(x) x[1] + x[2] - 2) optimlib_root(c(1.2, 1.3), function(x) c(sum(x^2) - 4, x[1] - x[2]))

title: Minimize an R function with OptimLib — optimlib
text: par Numeric vector starting values. fn Objective function minimize. Called fn(par, ...) must return single number. gr Gradient fn, called gr(par, ...) returning numeric vector length length(par). NULL, gradient-based methods use central finite differences. Ignored derivative-free methods. ... arguments passed fn, gr hess. method algorithm: "bfgs": BFGS quasi-Newton. "lbfgs": limited-memory BFGS, many parameters. "cg": nonlinear conjugate gradient. "gd": gradient descent, including momentum, Nesterov, AdaGrad, RMSProp, AdaDelta, Adam Nadam variants (see gd$method optimlib_control()). "newton": Newton's method; uses hess. support bounds. "nm": Nelder-Mead (derivative-free). "de", "de_prmm": differential evolution, variant population reduction multiple mutation strategies (derivative-free, global). "pso", "pso_dv": particle swarm optimization, differentially perturbed velocity variant (derivative-free, global). lower, upper Bounds parameters, recycled length(par). Use -Inf / Inf unbounded parameters. OptimLib handles bounds transforming parameters, par must lie strictly inside . hess Hessian fn method = "newton", called hess(par, ...) returning length(par) x length(par) matrix. NULL, approximated finite differences gradient. control list settings, result optimlib_control().

text: list elements: par: best parameter values found. value: fn evaluated par. success: TRUE OptimLib reports convergence. population methods meaningful check_freq (de / pso optimlib_control()) finite: default check_freq = Inf convergence test run, OptimLib reports TRUE "de" FALSE "de_prmm", "pso" "pso_dv" n_gen generations. Judge results value. iterations: number iterations (generations population methods). error: final value convergence criterion. method: method used.

title: RcppOptimLib (development version)
text: New optimlib(), general optim()-style interface minimizes plain R functions OptimLib’s unconstrained algorithms: BFGS, L-BFGS, conjugate gradient, gradient descent (including Adam related variants), Newton, Nelder-Mead, differential evolution (DE-PRMM) particle swarm (PSO-DV). Supports box constraints, ... arguments, finite-difference gradients Hessians none supplied. Population methods draw seed R’s RNG, set.seed() makes reproducible. New optimlib_sumt() minimization nonlinear inequality constraints, optimlib_root() systems nonlinear equations (Broyden’s method). New optimlib_control() exposes OptimLib’s convergence algorithm-specific settings, validation names values. optimlib_bfgs() optimlib_nm() now shortcuts optimlib(); results gain error method elements, callbacks now receive plain numeric vector instead one-column matrix. Fixed three bugs bundled OptimLib headers: L-BFGS stalled two iterations non-quadratic problems, PSO-DV failed runtime particle stagnated, SUMT used incorrect penalty gradient stopped short constrained optimum.
